summary.text: Emma Mendelsohn is The West Party's candidate for Laverton at the 2026 Victorian election. Her party page describes her as a business owner in Melbourne's west who employs young local people and trains them in a skilled trade, and says she has sat on the national board of a professional association and contributes to an industry advisory group of the Victorian Skills Authority. It adds that she started volunteering with the HIV/AIDS council many years ago.

prior_roles.role: National board director of a professional association

summary.text: Ghada Noune is the Liberal candidate for Laverton at the 2026 Victorian election. She is an accountant, and her party biography says her finance work has included helping business owners through periods of financial strain. She has also run a mobile food service for homeless people and raised money for families and orphanages.

summary.text: Jo Garcia is listed by the ABC as the Family First candidate for Laverton at the 2026 Victorian election, with no biography. Family First's website has no Laverton page for her; its only page under that name presents a Jo Garcia as the party's candidate for Gellibrand, a federal seat. That page describes someone born and raised in Melbourne who trained as a nurse and midwife and later worked in small business, real estate and community outreach.
summary.note: The Family First page names Gellibrand, not Laverton, and we could not confirm that it describes the Laverton candidate.

summary.text: Lucy Nguyen is the Greens candidate for Laverton at the 2026 Victorian election. A Vietnamese Australian, she represents Kororoit Creek Ward on Brimbank City Council. She has said that a childhood in public housing, followed by years of renting, shaped her priorities.

summary.text: Rufo Paredes is One Nation's candidate for Laverton at the 2026 Victorian election. He is chief executive of a migration agency and leads an organisation that promotes civic involvement among Filipino Australians. He contested Laverton as an independent in 2022, taking 1.0% of the primary vote. One Nation's page for him could not be read for this profile because the site refuses automated requests.

sources.title: Laverton: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Sarah Connolly is Labor's member for Laverton, a seat created in the redistribution before the 2022 election. She entered Parliament in 2018 as member for Tarneit and switched to Laverton in 2022. She has chaired the Public Accounts and Estimates Committee since 2023. She is recontesting Laverton in 2026.

summary.text: Shohre Mansouri Jajaee is the Animal Justice Party's candidate for Laverton at the 2026 Victorian election, as her party page and Wikipedia list her. A software engineer who has lived in Melbourne for about 20 years, she set up a charity in 2012 to help disadvantaged children get an education and ran it for six years, according to the party. An earlier listing of her on the party's Western Metropolitan Region upper-house ticket no longer appears on Wikipedia.

prior_roles.organisation: Charity supporting education for disadvantaged children (not named)
prior_roles.note: The party says she led it for six years and still mentors its team.

summary.text: Van Thanh Rudd is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Laverton at the 2026 Victorian election. An artist who also does maintenance work at a public school, he is a union member and coaches community soccer in Melbourne's west. He ran for the party in St Albans in 2022, and in 2010 he stood against Julia Gillard in the federal seat of Lalor for the unregistered Revolutionary Socialist Party. He is a nephew of former prime minister Kevin Rudd.

legal_and_integrity.text: Arrested with another man at an Australia Day protest; Wikipedia, citing ABC News, gives the offence as inciting a riot.
